newsitem.title: CANADA: Renaissance CEO admits to forecast mistake.
newsitem.headline: Renaissance CEO admits to forecast mistake.

text.p: Renaissance Energy Ltd Chief Executive Clayton Woitas, admitting he "screwed up big-time," said on Thursday he should have released weaker oil production forecasts in June when disappointing operating data began to surface.

Woitas, whose company's stock was pounded on Thursday following the release of the news, said he should have reported the lower expectations at the Canadian Association of Petroleum Producers' investment symposium last month.
"Why did we choose yesterday, July the 9th, to make the announcement? This is where I screwed up big-time," an emotional Woitas said on a conference call.

He said the company was on track to meet its 1997 average production target of 92,500 barrels of oil a day at the time of the company's annual meeting in late April, but disappointing second-quarter operating results were evident by the time of the mid-June CAPP conference.

"We were close to making that decision (to revise the projection) at that time. Only arrogance and stupidity and some not-yet-available data precluded me from making that decision," aknowledged Woitas.

Renaissance, long seen as one of Canada's most successful senior oil companies and a bellwether stock for the sector, said it revised downward its oil production projection for 1997 to 85,000 barrels a day from the previous figure.
The revelation sent Renaissance shares tumbling on Thursday. They were down 2.65 to 36.65 in midday trade.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's oil and gas subindex shed 84.56 points, or 1.21 percent, on Thursday after heavily weighted Renaissance's bad news.
The company's stock makes up 9.51 percent of the group.
The broad TSE 300 Composite Index was off just 0.04 percent on Thursday.
Peter Linder, analyst with CIBC Wood Gundy, said the company's reduced forecast was a big reason behind the sector's fall and may call into question expected operating results of other Canadian oils.

Despite the lower oil output projections, Woitas said in the conference call Renaissance did not change its 1997 earnings projection of C$130 million. At the company's annual meeting, it projected earnings of C$140 million.
He said the company raised its natural gas price expectation to C$1.90 per thousand cubic feet from C$1.75, which was expected to make up for the difference, he said.
He also said he did not expect any revisions to Renaissance's oil reserves in light of the operating situation and drilling was expected to remain on track.
Woitas said that instead of initially living with lower production expectations, when they became evident he placed pressure on the company's employees to meet the previous target.

"As my tension level increased, their tension level increased. This is not how we've built our company. We've built it based upon cutting out external influences and being in control," he said. "By racing to meet the ultimate number, that was put in jeopardy."

He said the company, which has increased its production mainly through drilling over the years, made the decision not to make an acquisition to fill in the 1997 production gap. ((Jeffrey Jones, Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
